topics.title: Biology, the microscope and the cell
topics.concept: Branches and characteristics of life, the light microscope and cell organelles.

subtopics.title: Branches of biology and characteristics of life
subtopics.concept: Adaptation enables organisms to survive in a particular environment. Branches: botany, zoology, ecology, cytology, evolution; the study of parasites is parasitology.

textbook_refs.section: 1.1.1 What is biology? – characteristics of living things

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 4 – Plants, Animals and the Environment

subtopics.title: The light microscope
subtopics.concept: Objective lens: brings the image into focus and magnifies it; eyepiece (ocular): magnifies; coarse/fine adjustment knobs focus; diaphragm controls light.

subtopics.title: Cell organelles
subtopics.concept: Textbook: centrioles and lysosomes are found only in animal cells; chloroplasts and cell walls only in plant cells. Rough ER is studded with ribosomes, which make proteins.

topics.title: Classification and diversity
topics.concept: Seven taxonomic ranks, binomial nomenclature, the five kingdoms, bacteria, invertebrates and plant groups.

subtopics.title: Taxonomic ranks, binomial names and the five kingdoms
subtopics.concept: Kingdom → phylum → class → order → family → genus → species. Scientific name = Genus + species (Equus caballus). Monera: prokaryotes; Protista: mostly unicellular/simple; Fungi: eukaryotes with extracellular digestion; Plantae: multicellular, cell walls, photosynthetic; Animalia: multicellular heterotrophs without cell walls.

textbook_refs.section: 2.1 The importance of classification – levels of classification

subtopics.title: Bacteria
subtopics.concept: Prokaryotes with cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleoid, pili and flagella. Diseases: tuberculosis, gonorrhoea, syphilis, anthrax, cholera (rabies is viral). Rhizobium in legume root nodules fixes nitrogen.

textbook_refs.section: 1.4.1 The structures and forms of bacteria
1.4.2 Economic importance of bacteria – bacterial diseases

subtopics.title: Invertebrates and plant groups
subtopics.concept: Cnidarians: radial symmetry, tentacles with stinging cells, two tissue layers. Dicot leaves have net (reticulate) venation; monocots parallel venation. Plant life cycles alternate between sporophyte and gametophyte generations.

topics.title: Nutrition, digestion, photosynthesis and respiration
topics.concept: Biomolecules and minerals, digestion and absorption, photosynthesis and aerobic respiration.

subtopics.title: Biomolecules, deficiency diseases and minerals
subtopics.concept: Carbohydrates contain C, H and O only. Fats are saturated or unsaturated according to the number of hydrogen atoms in their fatty acids. Marasmus: protein–energy deficiency. Magnesium deficiency: muscle weakness and cramps.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms
Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms

subtopics.title: Digestion and absorption
subtopics.concept: Mechanical (physical) digestion: taking in, moistening (lubrication), chewing, peristalsis. Chemical digestion: enzymatic hydrolysis. Absorption: nutrients pass from the intestine into the blood (fats into lacteals). Pancreas makes enzymes, liver makes bile, gall bladder stores bile.

textbook_refs.section: 1.3 Accessory organs – liver, gall bladder and pancreas
1.2.6 The small intestine – villi and lacteals

subtopics.title: Photosynthesis and aerobic respiration
subtopics.concept: Light reaction converts light energy into chemical energy; chlorophyll absorbs light. The dark reaction (light-independent) makes sugar from CO₂. Aerobic respiration uses glucose and oxygen.

textbook_refs.unit: Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms
Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms
Unit 3 – Metabolic Processes and Energy Transfers in Living Organisms

topics.title: Circulation, lymph and immunity
topics.concept: Heart and veins, blood groups and transfusion, lymphatic tissues and the immune system.

subtopics.title: Heart and blood vessels
subtopics.concept: The heart (size of a closed fist) lies in the thoracic cavity between the lungs; it is a double pump. Pericardial fluid between pericardium and heart reduces friction. Superior vena cava returns blood from the upper body, inferior vena cava from the lower body, to the right atrium.

textbook_refs.section: 2.2 Blood circulation – veins entering the right atrium

subtopics.title: ABO blood groups and transfusion
subtopics.concept: O is the universal donor, AB the universal recipient; A receives A and O, B receives B and O.

subtopics.title: Lymphatic tissues and immunity
subtopics.concept: Tonsils trap bacteria entering the throat. Antibodies are proteins made by lymphocytes (B cells) against antigens. The immune system defends the body against microbes, toxins and parasites.

topics.title: Respiratory and excretory systems
topics.concept: Airways and gas exchange; metabolic wastes and the kidney.

subtopics.title: Airways and alveolar air
subtopics.concept: Trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli. Fresh alveolar air after inhalation is rich in oxygen.

textbook_refs.section: 5.1 The respiratory tract – bronchi and bronchioles

subtopics.title: Metabolic wastes and the kidney
subtopics.concept: Main metabolic wastes in mammals: CO₂, excess water, salts, urea and red (bile) pigments. The loop of Henle lies in the medulla of the kidney.

textbook_refs.section: 6.2 The excretory organs – kidney and nephron

topics.title: Nervous system and sense organs
topics.concept: Neurons use electrical and chemical signals; the medulla controls reflexes; skin receptors and the ear.

subtopics.title: Neurons and the brain
subtopics.concept: Nerve impulses are electrical along the neuron and chemical (neurotransmitters) across synapses. The medulla oblongata controls breathing, heartbeat, coughing, swallowing and sneezing.

textbook_refs.section: 8.2 Parts of the human nervous system – medulla oblongata

subtopics.title: Skin and ear
subtopics.concept: The skin has receptors for touch, pressure, heat, cold and pain. The cochlea contains the receptors that send impulses along the auditory nerve.

topics.title: Endocrine and reproductive systems
topics.concept: Pituitary, thyroid and pancreatic hormones; puberty, gametes and the menstrual cycle.

subtopics.title: Hormones and endocrine glands
subtopics.concept: Prolactin stimulates milk production (oxytocin causes milk ejection). The thyroid is the largest endocrine gland and is critical to development and maturation. LH stimulates interstitial cells to release androgens. Hypoglycaemia = low blood sugar.

textbook_refs.section: 5.1.1 The need for homeostasis – blood sugar

subtopics.title: Puberty, gametes and the menstrual cycle
subtopics.concept: Male puberty: muscles, deep voice, broad chest and shoulders, facial hair (pelvis enlargement is female). Sperm mitochondria are in the middle piece. No ovum is available for fertilisation during the menstrual phase. Female organs: ovary, oviduct, uterus, cervix, vagina.

textbook_refs.section: 2.2 Male reproductive system – structure of the sperm

topics.title: Skeletal and muscular systems
topics.concept: Ossification, axial and appendicular skeleton, and the three muscle types.

subtopics.title: Bones and skeleton
subtopics.concept: Cartilage is converted to bone by ossification. Axial skeleton: skull, vertebral column, thorax (ribs, sternum); appendicular: limbs and girdles. Humerus = upper arm; femur = thigh.

subtopics.title: Muscle types
subtopics.concept: Smooth muscle: airways, gut, blood vessels, skin (not the heart – cardiac muscle). Skeletal muscles work in antagonistic pairs (flexor/extensor), have origin and insertion, and lift loads; peristalsis is done by smooth muscle.

topics.title: Plant systems
topics.concept: Plant tissues and organs, germination and plant hormones.

subtopics.title: Plant tissues and the shoot system
subtopics.concept: Simple tissues: parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma; complex tissues: xylem and phloem. Shoot system: stem, leaves, buds, flowers, fruits and seeds.

subtopics.title: Germination and plant hormones
subtopics.concept: The radicle emerges first during germination. Plant hormones are chemicals that act on target tissues, help the plant respond to the environment and can stimulate or inhibit growth.

topics.title: Nucleic acids and genetics
topics.concept: Transcription and protein synthesis, meiosis, Mendelian ratios and sex linkage.

subtopics.title: Transcription, protein synthesis and meiosis
subtopics.concept: mRNA is complementary and antiparallel to the DNA template (A→U, T→A, G→C, C→G). Protein synthesis in the cytoplasm needs mRNA, tRNA, rRNA/ribosomes – DNA stays in the nucleus. Meiosis produces gametes for sexual reproduction.

subtopics.title: Mendelian inheritance and sex linkage
subtopics.concept: Monohybrid cross: F₁ all dominant; F₂ phenotypic 3 : 1, genotypic 1 : 2 : 1. Haemophilia is X-linked recessive: a normal mother with a haemophiliac son is a carrier XᴴXʰ. Genotype = genetic make-up.

subtopics.title: Lamarckism and natural selection
subtopics.concept: Lamarck: use and disuse, inheritance of acquired characters. Darwin: over-production, variation, struggle for existence (competition), survival of the fittest, inheritance.

topics.title: Ecology and adaptation
topics.concept: Niches and relationships, decomposers, biomes, ecological pyramids and adaptations to the environment.

subtopics.title: Niches, symbiosis and decomposers
subtopics.concept: A niche is an organism's role, including when it is active. Mutualism: both partners benefit. Bacteria and fungi decompose dead organisms and recycle nutrients.

textbook_refs.section: 3.1 What is ecology? – habitat and niche

subtopics.title: Biomes and ecological pyramids
subtopics.concept: Grasslands: low rainfall with shrubs and small trees; deserts: very low rainfall. The pyramid of biomass compares biomass at each trophic level and narrows sharply from producers to carnivores.

subtopics.title: Adaptations to water and temperature
subtopics.concept: Xerophytes: thick epidermis, extensive roots, water-storage tissue, reduced leaf area, sunken stomata. Cold: insulation, shivering, small projections, good appetite, hibernation; heat: nocturnal behaviour, aestivation.
